content.jointProblem: Can uncertainty-aware spatial modelling link Pannonia’s farm policies to hail exposure more reliably than municipality-level ratings and identify potentially underpriced portfolio segments? The first experiment would test whether available weather inputs and independently verified locations and hail observations support field-level discrimination on held-out storms, before assessing any improvement in loss prediction.

rationale.text: Đukić has demonstrated climate downscaling in Vojvodina using satellite covariates and regression-kriging, providing a relevant methodological foundation rather than an already validated hail model.

sources.quote: Monthly mean air temperature fields at 1 km resolution were produced for the Vojvodina plain
with residuals subsequently interpolated by ordinary kriging.

rationale.text: His parcel-scale frost-risk work provides experience translating downscaled climate variables into geographically differentiated agricultural hazard indicators.

sources.quote: Maps produced at the parcel scale (0.5 ha) showed risk differentiation of up to 35 percentage points across elevation bands as narrow as 40 m
The index was validated against three independent frost event records with an accuracy of 81 %.

rationale.text: His work explicitly addresses prediction uncertainty, which is relevant when uncertain locations and weather estimates feed pricing decisions.

sources.quote: However, regression-kriging produced better-calibrated prediction intervals and smoother spatial fields in data-sparse mountain regions.
Uncertainty was quantified by propagating station observation errors and ERA-20C ensemble spread through the downscaling chain

rationale.text: His project record includes documented Python processing and geospatial service delivery, providing a practical starting point for an automated exposure-data workflow.

sources.quote: Core deliverables included the benchmark dataset of 18 agroclimatic indices (2001–2020), a Web Map Service interface, and a documented open-source Python processing chain.

constraints.text: Policy-location resolution must be established before field-level exposure assignment; settlement-only addresses cannot be treated as verified farm coordinates.

sources.quote: a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: The daily five-kilometre weather feed must undergo a hail-information and resolution audit; a finer output grid alone is not evidence of field-level hail accuracy.

sources.quote: We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
Vojvodina hailstorms are narrow and fast-moving

constraints.text: Validation and model complexity must respect the available three-year, approximately 1,200-policy dataset; spatially and temporally dependent claims must not be treated as independent validation events.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.

constraints.text: Delivery must fit the existing Python batch-pricing workflow and include a realistic operational handover to teams that also handle production support.

sources.quote: Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh
a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.

constraints.text: Methodological standards and publication rights must be agreed before data analysis starts.

sources.quote: prefers that methodological rigour and publication rights be explicitly agreed before project start.

constraints.text: The project must assign administrative coordination elsewhere rather than assume Đukić will take that role.

sources.quote: He is not seeking additional administrative coordination roles in the near term

risks: The supplied research demonstrates temperature, precipitation, frost and other agroclimatic modelling, not hail-intensity reconstruction or insurance pricing. Transfer to narrow, fast-moving hailstorms remains unvalidated and must be tested in the first experiment.

Daily five-kilometre inputs may contain insufficient information to recover field-level hail footprints. Availability, licensing and cost of independent hail observations or higher-resolution storm data are unknown.

Geo-tagged losses may not locate all insured assets or unclaimed policies accurately. Location error and missing non-claim exposure data could bias both validation and identification of underpriced segments.

Three claim years may contain too few independent severe storms for robust generalisation. The reported 18% excess does not establish that spatial hail exposure, rather than insured values, vulnerability or claims inflation, is the cause.
Operational integration could stall: the company’s previous flood-risk mapping prototype was completed but not integrated into pricing, and its technical teams have competing responsibilities.
Researcher availability, project budget, delivery timetable and data-access terms remain unknown; these could prevent execution despite open joint-project participation.
questions: What time commitment and start date can Đukić offer, and who will coordinate the project administratively?
Can Pannonia provide a policy-year exposure table including non-claims, insured values, coverage terms, asset or crop type, claims dates and amounts, and location-quality flags?
What do the existing loss geotags represent, and can policy locations be verified against insured parcels or buildings rather than settlement centroids?

Which hail-related variables, temporal aggregations and uncertainty information does MeteoVoj supply? Are event-level radar products, hail reports or other independent observations available and licensed for this use?

Can the first experiment use independently checked locations and storm observations, with entire storms or years held out, to compare municipality ratings, direct grid assignment and candidate downscaling methods?
What validation thresholds would justify proceeding, including location coverage, storm-level discrimination, uncertainty calibration and incremental loss-prediction performance?
What budget and deadline apply, who owns production integration and maintenance, and what output interface does the quarterly pricing pipeline require?
What privacy, security, weather-data licensing, publication, intellectual-property and actuarial approval requirements must be agreed before sharing data or changing rating factors?
